summary: PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17 extracts Yun–Zhang, Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017) 767–911; arXiv 1512.02683v3). Both recorded hashes reproduce, and the author's copy is byte-identical to the Annals PDF. The extraction has 43 items (7 planned, 36 missing), 5 routes and 37 source issues. I re-read the whole paper with three helper agents and verified every finding myself. The statements are faithful. I re-derived the review's main correction, E9 (Theorem 1.8 has 2^{r+1}), and the |ω_X| correction, and both are right. E1–E37 hold, except the third part of E28. There are 15 findings: 8 medium and 7 low. (1) Route 2 sends the function-field relative trace formula to GZ.5, which is a number-field theta-kernel stage. YZ19 puts the same orbital sums in the Part II, so the analytic side has split owners. (2) The queue merges every GlobalShtukas Part II into one job whose first member is Ciubotaru–Harris, so the special-cycles tranche can be deferred. (3) The Octahedron Lemma has two owners: SF.5 here and the Part II in YZ19/116. (4) Item 41 claims SF.5 plans Chow groups of stacks; it plans schemes only. (5) Item 42 claims FA.6 plans the Eisenstein spectral decomposition used in Theorem 4.3; nothing plans it over a function field. (6) The route reasons handed to the AL and GZ blueprint jobs still carry statements that E15, E17 and E9 show false. (7) Hadamard factorization has no item or owner. (8) Load-bearing geometric inputs have no item: the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula, Abel–Jacobi smoothness, Lang's theorem, cohomology of symmetric powers, Poincaré duality on DM stacks and Weil II weights. (9) Several analytic inputs planned elsewhere have no item. (10) Two new source issues and three minor slips: the dangling reference 'Lemma 7.15(3)' and an unargued step in the proof of Lemma 7.15. (11) E28's third part is not a misprint. (12) There is no sourceVersions field, so the collation worklist asks for the published text again. (13) The report says the libraries have nothing, but Tau Ceti's function-field divisor, Riemann–Roch and class-number API is missed. (14) Central-value positivity now has a GZ.5 node to link to. (15) Item-level slips.
checked: Independence. PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17 was written by Claude Code cc-fb70e5 (issue #1163, commit b997c73a, PR #1978, 22 September 2026). REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17 is by Claude Code cc-442dc5 (commit 67fc365e, PR #2523, 23 September 2026). There is no research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17.json. The paper's register section in research/errata/REGISTER.md was generated from the extraction. cc-f805bf appears nowhere in the result, the report, the review JSON, the review report or the register entries.

Disclosure. This session red-teamed BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 (PR #4725), whose route 1 is a member of the same GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands Part II group as this paper's route 1 (finding /2). That red team made no finding about the grouping. This session also wrote FIX-RT-AREA-iwasawa-1 (PR #4654), which edits GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights stages GZ.0, GZ.1, GZ.9 and adds a central-value positivity node at GZ.5 (/16). Finding /1 concerns GZ.5's field of definition, which that fix does not touch. Finding /14 relies on that fix. Finding /2 relies on the mechanism of RT-PAPER-BENOIST-19/1 (not my work, confirmed). Finding /8(a) and (f) point to the stacks Part II proposed by RT-AREA-etale/3 (not my work, confirmed, fix pending), which already covers the Deligne–Mumford trace formula and sheaf operations. I do not repeat that finding.

Versions (30 September 2026). https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.02683v3: SHA-256 76bb3576…ea1821ff, as recorded. The abstract page lists v1 (8 December 2015), v2 (5 January 2016) and v3 (11 April 2017), so v3 is the latest. The author's copy https://math.mit.edu/~zyun/Taylor_Expansion_published.pdf: SHA-256 b02ed5cb…c50fc111, as recorded. The Annals PDF https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v186-n3-p02-p.pdf has the identical hash. The Annals article page gives 'Received: 7 January 2016, Revised: 23 January 2017, Accepted: 5 April 2017, Published online: 12 September 2017' and links no correction. Crossref for 10.4007/annals.2017.186.3.2 has no update-to, updated-by or relation, and the filter updates:10.4007/annals.2017.186.3.2 returns 0 works.

The whole published paper (pp. 767–911), read through its text layer, with page images where superscripts mattered. Three read-only helper agents of this session read §§1–4, §§5–7 and §§8–9 with Appendices A–B line by line and reported candidates. I verified every finding myself at the quoted page: Proposition 2.4 and its proof (pp. 787–788), Theorem 4.3 and Proposition 4.5 (pp. 800–806), Proposition 3.1(2) and Proposition 3.2 (pp. 791–796), §3.3.1, Proposition 6.1 (p. 824), Lemma 6.7 (p. 830), Lemma 7.15 and §7.5 (pp. 866–867), Propositions 8.2 and 8.5 (pp. 869–873), Theorem 9.2 and §9.2–9.3 (pp. 875–879), §A.4.3 and Proposition A.12 (pp. 896–898), §B.1–B.2 (pp. 901–906), and the §1 statements of Theorems 1.1–1.8 (pp. 772–775).

Re-derived: E9, from definitions (2.1)–(2.9). On the orbits of [[0,1],[1,1]] and [[1,1],[1,0]] the K-conditions force xy ∈ O^× (so |xy|^s = 1) and give Σ_{E≥0}η(E) = L(η, 0) each, and w contributes 0. Hence J(∞, 1_K, s) = 2L(η, 0), J_r(1_K) = 2^{r+1}L^{(r)}(η, 0) for r > 0 even, and the r = 0 value 4L(η, 0) + q − 2. A helper independently confirmed this and the genus-2 check (184 against 368). E15 and E17 numerically: −0.12998 and −0.16012 at q = 3. E12's two repairs; E16 (also φ = s²); the smallness count in Proposition 8.2 (d − g + 1 > 2(g − 1)); and E28's third part (finding /11).

All 43 items against the text at their locators, with hypotheses (p > 2, X′ geometrically connected, r even, π unramified everywhere, the degree bounds d ≥ 2g′ − 1, max{2g′ − 1, 2g} and 3g − 2). The review's |ω_X| correction (Theorems 1.2 and 1.6 and Proposition 4.5 multiply by |ω_X|) is right. So are its corrections to items 1–3, 5, 9–11, 14, 16–18, 20, 22–29, 32, 33, 36, 37, 42 and 43. The numbered statements of the paper (Theorems 1.1–9.2, A.10, B.2, every lemma, proposition and corollary) are each covered by an item. The omissions are the unnumbered imports in findings /5, /7, /8 and /9.
All 37 sourceIssues were checked at their locators. E1–E7 and E9–E37 are correct, except E28's third part (finding /11). The review's rejection of E8 is right. New issues are in finding /10.

Statuses: every planned stage text read in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps: GS.0–GS.7, SF.3, SF.5, EDC.5, EDC.7, EDC.8, FA.1, FA.2, FA.5, FA.6, AL.1, AL.2, AL.3, DWP.7, DWP.8, GZ.5 and the GZ conventions, and AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0–AS.6 (number fields). Also the GS packet (65 nodes, partial), the AL packet (AL.2 not_read), the GZ packet (GZ.5 not_read) and the RT-AREA-etale fixes report on stacks (/3). Items 15, 38, 39, 40 and 43 are correctly planned in scope. Items 41 and 42 are not (findings /4, /5).

Routes, owners and dates. The extraction was merged on 22 September and the review on 23 September. No routed blueprint is finished: BP-GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands and BP-AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors are pending, BP-SchemeAndStackFoundations is external (issue #642), and the GZ, EDC and GS packets are partial with no YZ17 content. No cycle is created by the routes. Also checked: queue.json, make_queue.py (paper_designs, accepted_routes, ADDED_SOURCES) and the Part II group membership (finding /2).

Other extractions compared item by item on shared material: YUN-ZHANG-19 (240 items; routes 2, 7, 8), FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 (brief, items 24, 31, 32), LAFFORGUE-18 (GS routes), CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24/12 (stack Chow groups), BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19, CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26, YU-23, DADDEZIO-23, FENG-24, ABE-18, KLEVDAL-PATRIKIS-25 and GAN-HARRIS-SAWIN-ETAL-24 (Part II membership). Gross–Zagier 86 has no extraction in the repository. The duplicates found are the Octahedron Lemma (/3) and the analytic side (/1). YZ19/120 = YZ17/35 go to the same stage, which is consistent. The GS-packet nodes on Hecke correspondences (GS.2) and Hecke-finiteness (GS.3) are away from the legs and the bad places, so the whole-stack Hecke action of §§5.3 and 7.1 is not a duplicate.

Libraries at the pins (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474), searched in declarations.tsv, with every cited declaration read in its file. There are no hits for shtuka, Drinfeld, perverse, Chow, Gysin, Hecke algebra, Waldspurger or Satake. The Petersson, Eisenstein and symmetric-power hits concern classical modular forms and linear algebra. The function-field divisor API is in finding /13, Mathlib's Jensen formula and Tau Ceti's calculus hadamardFactor are in /7, and Tau Ceti AbelJacobi is weighted Abel–Jacobi classes on Weil divisors, not the Abel–Jacobi morphism of schemes.

Prerequisites: the 31 entries against the bibliography [1]–[31]. Only [21] (Sarnak's letter) and [28] (Yun's arithmetic fundamental lemma preprint) are omitted, and neither is load-bearing. [13] Kresch, Canonical rational equivalence, is listed as a prerequisite but cited by no item (finding /4).

Tooling: check_paper.py reports ok on the target. collation.py's provenance() returns 'preprint' for this record (finding /12). The PROTOCOL sections 0 and 15–18 and research/expansion/PROTOCOL.md were read before starting.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17.result.json route 2 (source → GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5; items 7, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14); route 1 brief ('GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5 for Waldspurger's period formula … this Part II needs only its conclusion, Theorem 4.7'); research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19.result.json routes 2 and 7
findings.claim: Route 2 sends the whole analytic side of the paper to GZ.5: Jacquet's regularized relative trace formula over the function field F = k(X), its finiteness theorems, the orbital sums J(u, f, s), the Eisenstein ideal and the spectral identity of Theorem 4.7. GZ.5 is a number-field stage. Its roadmap fixes 'a totally real field F, a CM quadratic extension K/F', and GZ.5 proves Waldspurger's formula by coherent theta kernels, importing MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–6 and the number-field AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.1–AS.4. Nothing in GZ.5 or its inputs builds automorphic forms, Eisenstein series or Poisson summation over a function field (FA.2, FA.6 are not among its dependencies). So a GZ blueprint either ignores this source, leaving items 7–14 without an owner, or enlarges GZ.5 to a second global-field theory by a different method. In both cases the Part II brief's import 'this Part II needs only its conclusion, Theorem 4.7' from GZ.5 fails: GZ.5 will not export an identity in E[q^{−s}, q^s] for PGL_2 over k(X). The route also splits one theory between two owners. The accepted PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 routes the same objects for its ramified generalization to the Part II: YZ19/218 'Orbital sum at an invariant u' (J(u, h, s_1, s_2), the definition in item 7 here), YZ19/226 (vanishing of the identity orbital integral, the §2.5 argument of item 8 here) and YZ19/133 are in YZ19 route 7. Conversely YZ19/149 is this paper's Lemma 9.1, which YZ17 routes to the Part II (item 28), while YZ19 sends it to GZ.5. The YZ19 review itself notes that 'GZ.5's description (coherent theta kernels, the Waldspurger formula) does not plan it'. Disclosure: this session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-iwasawa-1, which edits GZ stages (GZ.0, GZ.1, GZ.9, and a positivity node at GZ.5, finding /16). That fix does not change GZ.5's field of definition, and this finding does not depend on it.

findings.claim: Route 1 names the roadmap ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil, and its brief and the review rely on that id being shared with FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 and YUN-ZHANG-19. The queue never creates that id. paper_designs groups every accepted part-ii route by its parent alone. All accepted Part II routes with parent GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands become the single job DESIGN-GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsPartII (pending). The job is told 'if they split into independent directions, plan the first here and record a restructure proposal for the rest'. The accepted members, in registry order, are: CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26 (Ramanujan and Arthur weight constraints, 26 items), YU-23 (counting unramified local systems, 77), DADDEZIO-23 (crystalline companions, 1), YUN-ZHANG-19 (special cycles, 112), YUN-ZHANG-17 (special cycles, 22), FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 (special cycles, 25), FENG-24 (Tate cohomology of shtukas, 33), ABE-18 (crystalline companions, 17) and BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 (Ĝ-valued deformations, 22). These are at least six independent directions, and the first is the Ramanujan–Arthur one. So the special-cycle tranche of three papers (159 items, including every main theorem of this paper) can legitimately be deferred to a restructure proposal. The mechanism is the one confirmed in RT-PAPER-BENOIST-19/1. Disclosure: this session red-teamed BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 (PR #4725), whose route 1 is one of these members. That red team made no finding about the grouping.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17.result.json item PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/42 (status planned, FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.6); items 13 and 14
findings.claim: Item 42 says FA.6 plans 'the decomposition into cuspidal, residual and Eisenstein parts … and the Petersson inner product'. FA.6 plans automorphic functions, constant terms, cuspidal subspaces, their finiteness, Hecke correspondences and Satake. It does not plan Eisenstein series, their continuation or the spectral decomposition of the automorphic kernel. The only atlas owner of Eisenstein series and the spectral decomposition, AutomorphicSpectralTheory (AS.1–AS.4), is 'over number fields'. The proof of Theorem 4.3 (item 13), on which Theorem 4.7 and hence the main theorems depend, needs exactly this: the Eisenstein series E(g, φ, u, χ) 'defined as (the analytic continuation of)' the sum over B(F)\G(F), the kernel K_{f,Eis,χ} of (4.6), and Jacquet's spectral decomposition (4.8) K_f = K_{f,cusp} + K_{f,sp} + K_{f,Eis}, taken from [12, §7.1(4)]. No item states them, and nothing in the atlas plans them for a function field. Two further automorphic facts the paper uses are also unplanned and unitemised: that the everywhere unramified cusp forms are finite-dimensional, and multiplicity one, which gives 'Z_cusp is the set of unramified cuspidal automorphic representations' and dim W_π ≤ 1.
findings.evidence: FA.6 (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/FunctionFieldArithmetic.json): 'Construct G(K)\G(A_K), compact-level functions, central characters, constant terms and cuspidal subspaces. Prove reduction-theoretic finiteness of cuspidal spaces … Define Hecke correspondences and the unramified Satake dictionary with normalized Frobenius.' AutomorphicSpectralTheory summary: 'Develop the analytic structure of automorphic forms and L² automorphic representations for connected reductive groups over number fields. This covers Eisenstein series …'. Paper, proof of Theorem 4.3, pp. 800–801: 'To show this, we need to recall the Eisenstein series (cf. [12, §8.4]) … the Eisenstein series is defined as (the analytic continuation of) E(g, φ, u, χ) = Σ_{γ∈B(F)\G(F)} φ(γg, u, χ)'; p. 801: 'By [12, §7.1(4)], we have a spectral decomposition of the automorphic kernel function K_f defined by (2.3) (4.8) K_f = K_{f,cusp} + K_{f,sp} + K_{f,Eis}.' §7.4.2, p. 866: 'Let A_cusp ⊂ A be the finite-dimensional Q-vector space of cusp forms'; §9.3.1, p. 879: 'By Lemma 7.15, Z_cusp is the set of unramified cuspidal automorphic representations in A'.
findings.fix: In item 42, keep the automorphic functions, the Hecke algebra, Satake and cuspidal subspaces with their finiteness as planned at FA.6 (the GS packet node GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.0/cuspidal-automorphic-forms plans the same). Add a new missing item 'Eisenstein series for PGL_2 over a function field and the spectral decomposition of the automorphic kernel' (pp. 800–802: the induced family ρ_{χ,u}, E(g, φ, u, χ) with its continuation, K_{f,Eis} and (4.8)), and route it with the analytic side (per finding /1, route 1), or propose it as an addition to the pending DESIGN-FunctionFieldArithmeticPartII. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17.result.json route 5 reason (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.2) and route 2 reason; research/blueprint/make_queue.py ADDED_SOURCES
findings.claim: The review corrected items 9, 36 and 37 and the Part II brief, but not the source routes' reason texts. For a source route, the reason is the text the queue hands to the target blueprint job. Route 5's reason, which the AL blueprint job will receive, still states two things this extraction's own source issues show to be false. (a) 'Theorem B.2: for a nontrivial self-dual cuspidal π of GL_n(A), and assuming the Riemann hypothesis … every derivative of the normalized completed L-function is non-negative'. E15 shows this is false for n = 1 over a function field without the hypothesis that L(π, s) is entire. (b) 'the trivial representation is handled by passing to s(s−1)Λ(π, s) (Remark B.5)', which E17 shows is false over a function field. It also says Proposition B.1 'belongs with the Hadamard factorization AL.2's global theory already needs'. AL.2 plans no Hadamard factorization (finding /7). And it assigns Remark B.4's proof to FA.5, which no route names, so no FA job receives it. Route 2's reason, which the GZ job receives, quotes 'the explicit unramified computation J(u, 1_K, s) = L(η, 2s) + L(η, −2s) (Proposition 2.4)' with no restriction on u. findings.claim: Proposition B.1, and through it Theorem B.2 (super-positivity, the input that makes Theorem 1.7 unconditional), rests on Hadamard's factorization theorem. An entire function φ of finite order ρ has finite genus g, g ≤ ρ ≤ g + 1, and a canonical product φ(s) = s^m e^{h(s)}∏E_n(s/α_i). The paper takes this from Ahlfors §5.3.2, and the proof of Theorem B.2 also needs 'L(π, s) is entire of order one'. Item 36 mentions the theorem only as something the paper recalls. No item states it, route 5 claims AL.2 'already needs' it, and nothing in the atlas or the libraries has it. The only related library result is Mathlib's Jensen formula.

In particular, an entire function of finite order admits a product expansion of the form (B.1).' Proof of Theorem B.2, p. 904: 'The function L(π, s) is entire of order one'. findings.claim: Mistakes in the paper that no source issue records, each checked at the text. (a) Misprint, §9.2, p. 878 (also arXiv v3): 'By Lemma 7.15(3), Z_cusp(Q̄_ℓ) = Z^0_{0,ℓ}(Q̄_ℓ)'. Lemma 7.15 (p. 866) has only parts (1) and (2), and part (2) is exactly 'Z^0_{0,ℓ} = Z_{cusp,Q_ℓ}'. (b) Gap, proof of Lemma 7.15(1), p. 867. The step 'By (7.21), λ ∈ Z_Eis(Q̄), which means that the action of H on ϕ factors through Q[Pic_X(k)] via a_Eis, which is impossible' is given no argument. λ ∈ Z_Eis means λ(h_x) = χ(x) + q_xχ(x)^{−1} for a character χ of Pic_X(k). For χ = |·|^{−1/2}·ω with ω quadratic these values are real and within the Ramanujan range, so neither self-adjointness nor a size bound excludes them. What is needed is a genuine theorem: strong multiplicity one for isobaric representations (Jacquet–Shalika), or Drinfeld's GL_2 correspondence with Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt, as the paper itself does in Lemma 4.2. The conclusion is true, and Z^0_{0,ℓ} = Z_cusp, which §9 uses, depends on it. (c) Misprints: p. 862, proof of Lemma 7.11, 'which implies the proposition' for 'lemma'; p. 822, 'the the action'; p. 828, 'According the discussion' and 'According Theorem 6.5'.

findings.claim: E28 records as a misprint that on p. 824 'both … are smooth over X′_d of relative dimension d − g + 1' should read 'smooth over X̂′_d'. The printed statement is true, so it is not a misprint. X̂′_d → Pic^d_{X′} is a vector bundle of rank d − g′ + 1 for d ≥ 2g′ − 1, and Nm : Pic^d_{X′} → Pic^d_X is smooth of relative dimension g − 1 (its differential is the trace H¹(X′, O) → H¹(X, O), surjective when p > 2). So X̂′_d → Pic^d_X is smooth of relative dimension d − g + 1, and so is its base change X′_d ×_{Pic^d_X} X̂′_d → X′_d. At most, the sentence does not follow from the one before it. The argument written there proves smoothness over X̂′_d, which is what the review wrote in.
findings.evidence: p. 824: 'For d ≥ 2g′ − 1, the Abel-Jacobi map AJ_d : X′_d → Pic^d_{X′} is smooth of relative dimension d − g′ + 1, hence X′_d is smooth over Pic^d_X of relative dimension d − g + 1. Therefore, both X′_d ×_{Pic^d_X} X̂′_d and X̂′_d ×_{Pic^d_X} X′_d are smooth over X′_d of relative dimension d − g + 1.' (read at the text layer; g′ = 2g − 1, so d − g′ + 1 + (g − 1) = d − g + 1). E28's correction: 'smooth over X̂′_d'.
